acceptance_gate: A runs a frozen exploratory census with an independent check; B proves the characterization and its consequences; every census case agrees with the characterization or the disagreement is reported.
objective: Serves open question 3 of docs/KNOT_INTUITION.md (composition; 'composition across networks without groups remains open') under the source-aware reading. Chosen by the bounded direction scan recorded in the decision note, against 'space from native moves' (question 9), whose discriminator came out negative: for linear laws finite moves either vanish or grow like the substrate, so a static law can remove space but not create it. Background, not re-proved: degree-list colouring and Gallai trees (Gallai 1963; Borodin 1977; Erdos-Rubin-Taylor 1979). Standalone value: the first composition law for knots of a law that is not group-like. A witness network is a connected graph W of hidden vertices, each with exactly q neighbours once pendant leaves (the knot's variables) are added; the composite relation is the projection of proper q-colourings onto the leaves. A (exploratory census) computes the composite for every small connected W (q = 3 and 4) and compares it with the prediction that it passes K1-K3 exactly when W is a Gallai tree (every block a complete graph or an odd cycle), recording the knot types and cases outside the hypothesis. B proves the characterization, the knot types (trees give 'not all distinct'-type stars, cliques and odd cycles give 'not all equal'), that knots compose by gluing witness networks at a vertex exactly when no non-Gallai block is created, and the consequences for lattices (on bipartite substrates witness networks must be trees) and for nativity on the q-regular tree.
status: Complete 2026-10-20. In the q-colouring law, hidden witness networks with q neighbours per witness give their leaves a K1-K3 knot exactly when they are Gallai trees (K2, K3 automatic; classical degree-choosability read as a knot theorem); gluing fuses knots with multiplicative excluded mass; a shared visible vertex is a hub; native on regular trees wherever p* = 0. Census A (supported), proof B (proved), ledger Z. Recommendation: Research directions (knots as circuits, 1/3), deferred to the owner.
stop_rule: Stop after B. Stop earlier if the census contradicts the characterization within its hypothesis, or if prior work states the knot characterization.
title: Colouring knots compose along Gallai trees
